listening.title: Interview question: Tell me about a conflict in your team

lines.speaker: Ms. Lan (HR Manager)
lines.text: Quang, can you tell me about a time you handled a conflict in your team?

lines.speaker: Quang (Candidate)
lines.text: Sure. Last year, two developers on my team had a heated argument during a sprint meeting.

lines.speaker: Quang (Candidate)
lines.text: One thought the other was delaying his work. In fact, it was a miscommunication about the API deadline.

lines.speaker: Quang (Candidate)
lines.text: First, I suggested a short break to defuse the situation. Then I had a one-on-one chat with each of them.

lines.speaker: Ms. Lan (HR Manager)
lines.text: Did you take one person's side?

lines.speaker: Quang (Candidate)
lines.text: No, I stayed neutral. I listened to each perspective, then we met together and agreed on one shared deadline board.

lines.speaker: Ms. Lan (HR Manager)
lines.text: Did you need to escalate to the manager?

lines.speaker: Quang (Candidate)
lines.text: No. It was a win-win. They now work well together, and we had no missed deadlines after that.

questions.q: What was the real cause of the conflict?

options: He moved one developer to another team
They agreed on a shared deadline board

shadowing: Two teammates had a heated argument because of a miscommunication about the deadline.
First, I suggested a short break so everyone could calm down a little.
Then I had a one-on-one chat with each person to hear their perspective.
I stayed neutral and helped them agree on one shared deadline board.
As a result, we found a win-win solution and missed no deadlines after that.
